:::{#exr-local-vs-global-min}
#### A dip that is not the bottom

Let $f(x) = x^3 - 3x$ for $x \in \reals$.

1. Show that $f(x) - f(1) = (x - 1)^2 (x + 2)$.
2. Use part 1 to show that $f(x) \ge f(1)$
   for every $x$ in the interval $(0, 2)$.
3. Compute $f(-3)$.
   Is $f(1)$ the smallest value $f$ takes on all of $\reals$?
4. Does $f$ take a smallest value anywhere on $\reals$?

:::
